question_hindi: ___ प्रबंधन सूचना प्रणाली का एक महत्वपूर्ण कारक है।
question_english: ___ is an important factor of management information system.
technical_proof: MIS success depends jointly on the system framework, the data feeding it, and the processes acting on data.
explanation: System, Data, and Process are all foundational pillars of any MIS; none alone is sufficient.
trap_point: Students often pick only 'Data' since MIS is data-centric, ignoring System and Process.
memory_trick: Remember 'S-D-P' = System-Data-Process, the MIS tripod.
revision_fact: MIS = System + Data + Process working together.

question_hindi: निम्न में से Information gathering tool कौनसी है ___।
question_english: Which of the following is an Information gathering tool?
technical_proof: Standard fact-finding techniques used in requirement gathering include on-site observation, interviews, and document/form review — all are valid.
explanation: All three listed methods are recognized fact-finding techniques in SDLC's requirement gathering phase.
trap_point: Some students think only 'Interviews' counts as formal gathering; observation and document review are equally valid.
memory_trick: Fact-finding techniques: Interview, Observation, Questionnaire, Record review.
revision_fact: Fact-finding techniques = Interviews + Observation + Document Review + Questionnaires.

question_hindi: निम्न में से Feasibility analysis का प्रकार नहीं है ___।
question_english: Which of the following is NOT a type of Feasibility analysis?
technical_proof: The recognized types of feasibility are Technical, Economic, Operational, Schedule, Legal, and sometimes Social feasibility. 'Data feasibility' is not a standard category.
explanation: 'Data feasibility' is not part of the standard feasibility taxonomy (TELOS: Technical, Economic, Legal, Operational, Schedule).
trap_point: Students confuse this with 'Technical feasibility' which does cover data/hardware needs.
memory_trick: Use 'TELOS' to recall real feasibility types: Technical, Economic, Legal, Operational, Schedule.
revision_fact: Feasibility types (TELOS) never include 'Data feasibility' as a standalone category.

question_hindi: बुद्धिशीलता (Brainstorming) में कितने चरण होते हैं?
question_english: How many phases are there in Brainstorming?
technical_proof: Brainstorming is generally conducted in 3 phases: idea generation, idea clarification, and idea evaluation.
explanation: Standard SAD textbooks describe brainstorming as a 3-phase group technique for requirement elicitation.
trap_point: Some confuse this with the 4 stages of a general problem-solving cycle.
memory_trick: 3 phases = Generate → Clarify → Evaluate.
revision_fact: Brainstorming has 3 phases: Generation, Clarification, Evaluation.

question_hindi: शीर्ष प्रबंधन के उपयोग के लिए रणनीतिक स्तर पर ___ स्तर की आपूर्ति की जानकारी देता है।
question_english: ___ level supplies information to strategic tier for the use of top management.
technical_proof: In the classic 3-tier MIS pyramid (Operational, Tactical, Strategic), the Tactical (middle-management) level feeds summarized information upward to the Strategic tier.
explanation: Operational level handles day-to-day transactions; Tactical level aggregates and reports to Strategic/top management.
trap_point: Students often mix up 'Operational' and 'Tactical' — Operational feeds Tactical, not directly Strategic.
memory_trick: Pyramid flow: Operational → Tactical → Strategic (bottom to top).
revision_fact: MIS pyramid: Operational (bottom) → Tactical (middle) → Strategic (top).

question_hindi: एक DFD में बाहरी संस्थाओं (external entities) को ___ द्वारा दर्शाया जाता है।
question_english: In a DFD, external entities are represented by a ___.
technical_proof: Standard Gane-Sarson/Yourdon DFD notation: Rectangle/Square = External Entity, Circle/Rounded = Process, Open rectangle = Data Store, Arrow = Data Flow.
explanation: This is a fixed DFD notation convention taught in every SAD syllabus.
trap_point: Frequently swapped with 'Circle' (which represents a Process, not an entity).
memory_trick: Rectangle = Entity (outside), Circle = Process (inside), Open box = Store, Arrow = Flow.
revision_fact: DFD notation: Rectangle = External Entity.

question_hindi: Model elements के समूह को क्या कहा जाता है?
question_english: A group of model elements is called?
technical_proof: None of the OCR-transcribed options ('Process moment', 'Package members', 'Packet manage', 'Package moments') are valid UML/SAD terminology. The correct standard term for a group of model elements in UML is simply a 'Package'.
explanation: This question's options appear corrupted by OCR. In UML, a Package is the container construct used to group related model elements together.
trap_point: Do not memorize the garbled options as-is; recall that the real UML term is 'Package'.
memory_trick: Package = folder that groups UML model elements.
revision_fact: In UML, 'Package' is the mechanism for organizing/grouping model elements.

question_hindi: अनुक्रमिक संख्याओं (Serial numbers) का उपयोग कोड के रूप में किया जाता है, ये हैं-
question_english: Serial numbers used as codes are-
technical_proof: Serial/sequential codes (1,2,3...) are Concise (short) and Expandable (can keep adding numbers), but they are NOT inherently Meaningful (the number itself carries no descriptive info) nor especially Comprehensive.
explanation: (i) Concise and (iii) Expandable are true properties of serial codes; (ii) Meaningful and (iv) Comprehensive are not.
trap_point: Students assume all 'good code' properties (meaningful, comprehensive) apply to every code type — they don't for pure serial numbering.
memory_trick: Serial codes: short & extendable, but 'blind' (no meaning).
revision_fact: Serial/sequential codes are concise and expandable, but not meaningful.

question_hindi: ___ को डेटा के रूप में परिभाषित किया जा सकता है जिसे एक ऐसे रूप में संसाधित किया गया है जो प्राप्तकर्ता के लिए सार्थक है।
question_english: ___ can be defined as data that has been processed into a form that is meaningful to the recipient and is of real or perceived value in current or prospective decisions.
technical_proof: This is the textbook definition of 'Information' — data becomes information only after processing that adds meaning and decision value.
explanation: Data = raw facts; Information = processed, meaningful, decision-relevant data. This is the classic Davis & Olson definition.
trap_point: Some confuse 'Data' and 'Information' — Data is raw/unprocessed, Information is the processed output.
memory_trick: Data + Processing + Meaning = Information.
revision_fact: Information = processed data with meaning/value for decision-making.

question_hindi: किस प्रकार की Feasibility में hardware के configuration पर system के लिए अधिक महत्व दिया जाता है?
question_english: Which type of Feasibility gives more importance to hardware for system configuration?
technical_proof: Technical feasibility evaluates whether the required hardware, software, and technology are available/adequate to build the system.
explanation: Technical feasibility directly examines hardware/software capability and configuration requirements.
trap_point: Note the duplicate option (a) and (d) 'Social feasibility' in the source — likely an OCR/printing duplication error; does not affect the correct choice (b).
memory_trick: Technical = Tech stack, hardware, software capability check.
revision_fact: Technical feasibility = hardware/software adequacy check.
ocr_confidence: Medium - duplicate option (a)/(d) in source, likely printing error

question_hindi: Operational Feasibility का मुख्य सम्बन्ध किससे है-
question_english: Operational Feasibility is mainly concerned with-

options.text: Giving more importance to hardware in evaluation

technical_proof: Operational feasibility assesses whether the proposed system will work within the existing organizational, human, and political environment — i.e., whether people will actually use and accept it.
explanation: It examines organizational culture, staff willingness, political resistance, and human factors around adoption.
trap_point: Confused with Technical feasibility, which deals with hardware; Operational is about people/organization acceptance.
memory_trick: Operational = will people actually USE it?
revision_fact: Operational feasibility = human, organizational, political acceptance of the system.

question_hindi: एक System है-
question_english: A System is-

options.text: आपस में dependent units का समूह
किसी विशेष लक्ष्य की प्राप्ति हेतु विभिन्न Components जोड़ना
System विभिन्न Components से मिलकर बना होता है

technical_proof: A system is an organized set of interdependent, interacting components working together toward a common goal — all three statements describe valid facets of a system.
explanation: Standard systems theory: interdependence + component integration + goal orientation are all defining traits.
trap_point: Students may pick only one partial definition instead of recognizing all are complementary.
memory_trick: System = Interdependent + Integrated + Goal-driven components.
revision_fact: A system = group of interdependent components working toward a common goal.

question_hindi: Block codes हैं-
question_english: Block codes are-
technical_proof: Block codes assign a reserved range/block of numbers to a category, making them Meaningful (blocks map to categories) and Expandable (room within/between blocks for new entries).
explanation: (ii) Meaningful and (iii) Expandable correctly describe block codes; they are not necessarily the most 'Concise' or 'Comprehensive' among coding types.
trap_point: Don't confuse with Serial codes (Q8) which are Concise+Expandable; Block codes are Meaningful+Expandable.
memory_trick: Block code = reserved range per category = Meaningful + Expandable.
revision_fact: Block codes are meaningful and expandable.

question_hindi: निम्न में से flow chart का प्रकार नहीं है-
question_english: Which of the following is NOT a type of flow chart?
technical_proof: 'Square chart' is not a recognized chart type. Bar, Line, and Pie charts are all standard data visualization/flow-chart-family chart types.
explanation: This is a straightforward elimination question — 'Square chart' does not exist as a standard chart classification.
trap_point: Watch for fictitious-sounding distractor terms invented purely for the exam ('Square chart').
memory_trick: If a chart name sounds made-up, it's the odd one out.
revision_fact: Bar, Line, Pie are real chart types; 'Square chart' is not.

question_hindi: Relation तथा Speed को diagram में प्रदर्शित करने के लिए किसका उपयोग करते हैं-
question_english: Which is used to display Relation and Speed in a diagram?
technical_proof: A Chart (e.g., line/graph chart) is the standard visual tool used to depict relationships and rates/speed of change between variables.
explanation: Charts visually represent relationships and trends (like speed of change) between data points.
trap_point: 'Box' and 'Square' are structural shapes, not analytical display tools — easy to eliminate.
memory_trick: Speed/relation → think 'graph/Chart', not a shape.
revision_fact: Charts are used to represent relationships and speed/trends of data.

question_hindi: पुरानी प्रणाली की तरह ही नई प्रणाली का उपयोग करके परिणामों की तुलना करने के लिए इसे ___ के रूप में जाना जाता है।
question_english: Use the new system at the same time as the old system to compare the results. This is known as ___.
technical_proof: Running old and new systems together and comparing outputs is the definition of Parallel Run/Parallel Operation conversion strategy.
explanation: This is one of the four system conversion strategies: Direct, Parallel, Pilot, and Phased.
trap_point: Students confuse this with 'Simultaneous processing' (a computing term unrelated to system conversion strategy).
memory_trick: Old + New running together to compare = Parallel Operation.
revision_fact: Parallel Operation = running old & new systems together to validate results before full cutover.

question_hindi: Design चरण के बाद तैयार किए गए दस्तावेज़ को ___ के रूप में जाना जाता है।
question_english: After the design phase, the document prepared is known as ___.
technical_proof: The output document of the Design phase is naturally termed the 'Design Specification' — it details how the system will be built.
explanation: Each SDLC phase produces a matching-named specification document (requirement specification, design specification, etc.).
trap_point: Don't confuse with 'system specification' (broader, earlier-stage document from requirements analysis).
memory_trick: Design phase output = Design Specification (name matches the phase).
revision_fact: The design phase produces the Design Specification document.

question_hindi: निम्न कॉलम A व कॉलम B का मिलान कीजिए- a.Technical Feasibility, b.Operational Feasibility, c.Economic Feasibility, d.Social Feasibility
question_english: Match Column A with Column B — a.Technical Feasibility, b.Operational Feasibility, c.Economic Feasibility, d.Social Feasibility
technical_proof: Correct mapping: Technical→(iii) Hardware configuration importance; Operational→(i) done by small groups of people; Economic→(ii) cost/benefit determination; Social→(iv) general public acceptance.
explanation: Each feasibility type is matched to its defining concern as per standard SAD theory.
trap_point: Easy to mismatch Technical and Operational since both start with process-oriented wording in Hindi.
memory_trick: T-Hardware, O-People(small group), E-Cost/Benefit, S-Public acceptance.
revision_fact: Match feasibility type to its core concern: Technical=Hardware, Operational=People, Economic=Cost/Benefit, Social=Public acceptance.

question_hindi: कौनसी Feasibility में Cost/benefit analysis किया जाता है-
question_english: In which Feasibility is Cost/benefit analysis done?
technical_proof: Cost/Benefit analysis is the defining activity of Economic feasibility — it weighs project cost against expected benefit.
explanation: Economic feasibility = quantifying and comparing costs vs. benefits of the proposed system.
trap_point: None — this is a clean, direct-fact question with no real distractor risk.
memory_trick: Economic = Money in vs money out (Cost/Benefit).
revision_fact: Economic feasibility centers on cost-benefit analysis.

question_hindi: एक System में डेटाबेस बनाने का कार्य कौन करता है-
question_english: Who carries out the task of building the database in a System?
technical_proof: Programmers implement the physical database structures based on the design provided by the analyst.
explanation: Analysts design logical structures; Programmers implement/build the actual database.
trap_point: Common trap: confusing 'Analyst' (designs) with 'Programmer' (implements/builds).
memory_trick: Analyst designs, Programmer builds.
revision_fact: Database building/implementation is a Programmer's task, not the Analyst's.

question_hindi: Economic feasibility का मुख्य उपयोग क्या है-
question_english: What is the main use of Economic feasibility?
technical_proof: Economic feasibility is used to (i) determine expected cost/benefit from proposed system, (ii) decide whether to design & implement if profitable, and (iii) assess if it's an ongoing beneficial effect — all three are valid economic feasibility uses.
explanation: Statement (iv), about being done by 'a small group of people', describes Operational feasibility, not Economic, so it is excluded.
trap_point: Watch for a plausible-sounding 4th statement that actually belongs to a different feasibility type (mixing categories).
memory_trick: Only include statements that are truly about cost/benefit, not about who performs it.
revision_fact: Economic feasibility = cost/benefit identification + go/no-go decision + assessing ongoing benefit.

question_hindi: किस प्रकार की feasibility में यह देखा जाता है कि प्रस्तावित Project उस सामान्य व्यक्ति को स्वीकार्य हो या नहीं-
question_english: In which feasibility is it checked whether the proposed Project is acceptable to the common/general person?
technical_proof: Social feasibility evaluates whether the general public/end-users will accept and be comfortable with the proposed system.
explanation: This is the definitional focus of Social feasibility — user/public acceptance, distinct from legal compliance or management approval.
trap_point: Confused with Legal feasibility (compliance with laws) or Management feasibility (approval by managers).
memory_trick: Social = will ORDINARY PEOPLE accept it?
revision_fact: Social feasibility = general public acceptance of the proposed system.

question_hindi: समूह वर्गीकरण कोड (Group classification codes) हैं-
question_english: Group classification codes are-
technical_proof: Group classification codes divide items into meaningful, expandable groups — matching properties (ii) Meaningful and (iv) Comprehensive as per the book's key.
explanation: Per the answer key, options ii and iv (Meaningful and Comprehensive) are the defining traits selected for this code type.
trap_point: The OCR text for this item's options is partially garbled; treat with some caution and cross-check against your printed source if available.
memory_trick: Group classification code → think 'meaningful categories, comprehensive coverage'.
revision_fact: Group classification codes emphasize being meaningful and comprehensive.

question_hindi: एक Data flow कर सकता है ___।
question_english: A data flow can ___.

options.text: Only emanate from an external entity
Only terminate in an external entity
May emanate and terminate in an external entity
May either emanate or terminate in an external entity but not both

technical_proof: Standard DFD rule: a single data flow arrow either originates from an external entity and goes into the system, OR originates in the system and goes to an external entity — not both directions in the same flow.
explanation: This mirrors the DFD rule that data cannot flow directly between two external entities either — flows to/from entities are one-directional per arrow.
trap_point: Students often think a flow can freely go both ways between entity and system in one arrow — it cannot; each flow has one direction.
memory_trick: One flow, one direction: entity→system OR system→entity, never both.
revision_fact: A data flow connects to an external entity in only one direction at a time.

question_hindi: ___ को कंप्यूटर की समस्याओं को हल करने के लिए सबसे हालिया और शायद सबसे व्यापक तकनीक के रूप में परिभाषित किया जा सकता है।
question_english: ___ can be defined as the most recent and perhaps the most comprehensive technique for solving computer problems.
technical_proof: System Analysis is described in textbooks as the comprehensive, structured technique/methodology for solving organizational/computer-based problems.
explanation: This is a definitional statement directly associated with the discipline of System Analysis.
trap_point: Distractors ('System Data', 'System Record') are not methodologies at all — easy to eliminate with basic reasoning.
memory_trick: 'Comprehensive technique to solve problems' = System Analysis (the discipline itself).
revision_fact: System Analysis is framed as the most comprehensive problem-solving technique in computing.

question_hindi: SDLC का अर्थ ___ है।
question_english: SDLC stands for ___.
technical_proof: SDLC universally stands for 'System Development Life Cycle' in software/systems engineering.
explanation: This is a fixed, well-known acronym with no ambiguity.
trap_point: Distractor options swap 'Development' with 'Design' — read carefully, SDLC is about the full development lifecycle, not just design.
memory_trick: SDLC = System DEVELOPMENT Life Cycle (not 'Design').
revision_fact: SDLC = System Development Life Cycle.

question_hindi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सूचना की विशेषता है/हैं?
question_english: Which of the following is/are Characteristics of information?
technical_proof: Good information is characterized by Accuracy, Relevance, appropriate Form, Timeliness, Completeness, and clear Purpose — all listed traits are valid characteristics.
explanation: Standard SAD/MIS texts list these as the core quality dimensions of 'good information'.
trap_point: Students might pick only one pair thinking others are less important — but all are commonly cited jointly.
memory_trick: Good info = ARFTCP: Accuracy, Relevance, Form, Timeliness, Completeness, Purpose.
revision_fact: Quality of information is judged by accuracy, relevance, form, timeliness, completeness, and purpose.

question_hindi: The data Flow Diagram किस system का मूल घटक है।
question_english: The data Flow Diagram is the basic component of ___ system.
technical_proof: A DFD models WHAT the system does (data and processes) without regard to HOW it's implemented — this makes it a component of the Logical system view, not the Physical.
explanation: Logical DFDs describe business processes/data flow abstractly; Physical DFDs (a separate concept) add implementation details like devices and file formats.
trap_point: Easy to confuse with 'Physical' since DFDs can also be drawn as 'Physical DFDs' — but the DFD technique itself is fundamentally a logical modeling tool.
memory_trick: DFD = Logical modeling tool (what, not how).
revision_fact: DFD is fundamentally a logical system modeling component.

question_hindi: ___ में मौजूदा प्रक्रियाओं और सूचना प्रवाह की समीक्षा शामिल है।
question_english: ___ includes review of the existing procedures and information flow.
technical_proof: The Feasibility Study stage involves reviewing current procedures and information flow to judge if a new system is viable and needed.
explanation: Feasibility Study is the early SDLC stage that examines the existing system's workflow before deciding to proceed.
trap_point: Confused with 'System analysis', which goes deeper into requirements after feasibility is approved.
memory_trick: Feasibility Study = early review of 'as-is' procedures/info flow.
revision_fact: Feasibility Study reviews existing procedures and information flow before project approval.

question_hindi: Organization chart ___ का एक प्रकार है।
question_english: Organization chart is a type of ___.
technical_proof: An organization chart displays reporting relationships in a tree/hierarchy form, making it a type of Hierarchical chart.
explanation: Org charts represent superior-subordinate structure — inherently hierarchical in nature.
trap_point: IPO chart (Input-Process-Output) is a different tool entirely used for process/module documentation, not org structure.
memory_trick: Org chart = tree of authority = Hierarchical chart.
revision_fact: Organization charts are a type of hierarchical chart.

question_hindi: निम्नलिखित कॉलम A या कॉलम B का सही से मिलान कीजिए- a.Management Feasibility, b.Legal Feasibility, c.Social Feasibility(i), d.Social Feasibility(ii)
question_english: Match Column A with Column B — a.Management Feasibility, b.Legal Feasibility, c.(Social/Economic) Feasibility, d.Social Feasibility
technical_proof: Correct mapping per key: Management→(ii) whether project will finish within given time, Legal→(iii) whether project follows all rules/regulations, and the remaining two Social-labelled rows map to (i) small-group acceptance and (iv) general-person acceptance respectively.
explanation: The source table appears to duplicate 'Social Feasibility' as both category c and d — likely an OCR/print duplication of what should be two distinct feasibility types (e.g., one may actually be 'Economic Feasibility').
trap_point: Do not take the duplicate 'Social Feasibility' labels at face value; focus on matching the descriptive statements (i)-(iv) correctly as per the answer key.

revision_fact: Match statements carefully — printed category labels can repeat due to OCR/print errors; verify against original source book if precision is critical.

question_hindi: Data दो Data stores के बीच प्रवाहित नहीं हो सकता क्योंकि ___?
question_english: Data cannot flow between two data stores because ___?

options.text: it is not allowed in DFD
a data store is a passive repository of data

technical_proof: A data store is a passive repository — it cannot actively move or push data; a process is required to read from one store and write to another.
explanation: Since data stores have no active behavior (they just hold data), any transfer between them must go through a Process, which is why direct store-to-store flow is disallowed.
trap_point: Students often just memorize 'not allowed in DFD' (option a) without understanding WHY — the real reason is passivity of data stores.
memory_trick: Stores are passive; only Processes are active and can move data.
revision_fact: Data cannot flow directly between two data stores because stores are passive, not active, elements.

question_hindi: Logical DFD's के लिए सत्य कथन है-
question_english: True statement(s) for Logical DFD's-
technical_proof: Statement (i) is true: Logical DFDs show data flow from a business-control/user perspective. Statement (ii) is false: checking HOW the data flow is implemented technically is the concern of Physical DFDs, not Logical DFDs.
explanation: Logical DFD = 'what' the business does with data (true for i); it does NOT address implementation/how it's applied in the system (so ii is false).
trap_point: Easy to mistakenly mark both true since both statements 'sound' related to DFDs — but statement (ii) actually describes Physical DFD's job.
memory_trick: Logical = What/Why (business view); Physical = How (implementation view).
revision_fact: Logical DFDs represent the business/user view of data flow, not the technical implementation.

question_hindi: निम्न में से उच्चतम level का Data flow diagram कौनसा है-
question_english: Which of the following is the highest level Data flow diagram?
technical_proof: Level 0 (the Context Diagram) is the highest/most abstract level of a DFD, showing the entire system as a single process; higher numbers (1,2,3) represent increasing decomposition detail, not higher abstraction.
explanation: DFD numbering works opposite to intuition: Level 0 is the topmost/most abstract, and each increasing level number means MORE detail/lower abstraction.
trap_point: Very common trap — students assume 'Level 3' is 'highest' because the number is bigger, but it's actually the most detailed/lowest-level diagram.
memory_trick: Level 0 = top view (Context Diagram); higher levels = more zoomed-in detail.
revision_fact: Level 0 DFD (Context Diagram) is the highest/most abstract level.

question_hindi: अच्छी तरह से डिजाइन किए गए सिस्टम की विशेषताएँ निम्नलिखित में से हैं-
question_english: The characteristics of a well-designed system are among the following-

options.text: A, B, C, D and E
A, B, C, D, E and F

technical_proof: A well-designed system is Practical, Effective, Secure, Reliable, Flexible, and Economical — all six listed traits (A-F) are valid characteristics.
explanation: Standard SAD texts list these six qualities together as hallmarks of good system design.
trap_point: Students might exclude 'Economical' (F) thinking cost isn't a 'design' quality — but cost-efficiency is indeed considered a design characteristic.
memory_trick: PESRFE: Practical, Effective, Secure, Reliable, Flexible, Economical.
revision_fact: A well-designed system is practical, effective, secure, reliable, flexible, and economical.

question_hindi: संरचित चार्ट (Structured charts) ___ का उत्पाद हैं?
question_english: Structured charts are a product of?
technical_proof: Structured charts (module hierarchy diagrams) are produced during the Structured Design phase, showing module decomposition and control flow.
explanation: Structured design translates data-flow/logical analysis into a hierarchical module structure represented by structure charts.
trap_point: Confused with 'requirements analysis' — analysis produces DFDs, not structure charts; structure charts belong to the Design stage.
memory_trick: DFD = Analysis output; Structure Chart = Design output.
revision_fact: Structure charts are produced during the design phase, not analysis.

question_hindi: ___ सिस्टम प्रोजेक्ट से संबंधित जानकारी के संग्रह को संदर्भित करता है।
question_english: ___ refers to the collection of information pertinent to systems Project.
technical_proof: Collecting information relevant to a systems project is, by definition, 'Data Gathering' (a core requirement elicitation activity).
explanation: This is a direct terminology-matching question.
trap_point: Distractors like 'Data transfer' and 'Data Embedding' are unrelated technical terms, easily eliminated.
memory_trick: Collecting project-relevant info = Data Gathering.
revision_fact: Data gathering = collecting information relevant to the systems project.

question_hindi: ___ किसी कंपनी या कार्यों की श्रृंखला के माध्यम से डेटा के प्रवाह को परिभाषित करता है जो कंप्यूटरीकृत प्रसंस्करण का प्रतिनिधित्व कर सकते हैं या नहीं भी कर सकते हैं।
question_english: ___ gives defining the flow of data through an organization or a company or series of tasks that may or may not represent computerized processing.
technical_proof: A System Flowchart depicts the flow of data and documents through an organization's processes, whether or not those processes are computerized.
explanation: This distinguishes System Flowcharts (org-level, can include manual steps) from Program Flowcharts (purely computerized logic).
trap_point: Don't confuse with 'System process' which is not a standard diagramming tool name.
memory_trick: System Flowchart = data flow across the whole org, manual or computerized.
revision_fact: System flowchart shows data flow across an organization, computerized or not.

question_hindi: Management Feasibility का कार्य क्या है-
question_english: What is the function of Management Feasibility?
technical_proof: Management feasibility covers: (i) checking if management accepts the project, (ii) analyst treating it as non-feasible if management rejects it, and (iii) some organizations needing centralized control — all three points are valid aspects.
explanation: All listed statements describe legitimate facets of how management approval/attitude affects feasibility assessment.
trap_point: Students may exclude the 'centralized control' point (iii) as unrelated, but it is included as a valid organizational factor.
memory_trick: Management feasibility = Does leadership approve, and how centralized is control?
revision_fact: Management feasibility assesses organizational leadership's acceptance and control needs for the project.

question_hindi: System design का मुख्य कार्य क्या है-
question_english: What is the main function of System design?

options.text: System में आवश्यक सुधार, सुरक्षा व नियंत्रण की Design बनाना
समस्त data flow को बनाया जाता है
System में input क्या होंगे, उनका flow क्या होगा

technical_proof: System design covers designing improvements/security/control mechanisms, mapping out all data flows, and defining inputs and their flow — all are core system design functions.
explanation: System design translates analysis output into a concrete blueprint covering control, data flow, and input/output specification.
trap_point: Each option alone captures only part of system design's scope; the exam wants recognition that all are part of the same overall activity.
memory_trick: System design = Security/Control + Data Flow + Input Design, all combined.
revision_fact: System design's main function spans security/control design, data flow design, and input specification.

question_hindi: तार्किक design जो कागज के ऊपर तैयार किया जाता है, उसे वास्तविक कार्यशील रूप में ढालना-
question_english: Converting the logical design prepared on paper into an actual working form is-
technical_proof: Physical Design is the process of converting an abstract logical design into a concrete, working, implementation-ready form (files, programs, hardware specifics).
explanation: Logical Design = 'what' on paper; Physical Design = 'how' it actually gets implemented/built.
trap_point: Reverse of Q28 concept — here Logical is the 'paper' stage, and moving to real implementation is Physical.
memory_trick: Paper plan → Working system = Physical Design.
revision_fact: Physical Design converts the logical (paper) design into a real, working system.

question_hindi: किस प्रक्रिया द्वारा पता लगाया जाता है कि Project सभी अधिनियमों एवं Legal rules को follow कर रहा है या नहीं-
question_english: Which process determines whether the Project is following all acts and Legal rules?
technical_proof: Legal feasibility specifically checks compliance of the proposed system/project with applicable laws, acts, and regulations.
explanation: This is the definitional purpose of Legal feasibility in the TELOS framework.
trap_point: Straightforward — 'acts and legal rules' directly signals Legal feasibility, minimal distractor risk.
memory_trick: Legal rules/acts = Legal feasibility, always.
revision_fact: Legal feasibility verifies compliance with applicable laws and regulations.

question_hindi: System test plan कब निर्दिष्ट किया जाता है?
question_english: When is the System test plan specified?

options.text: जब अंतिम विनिर्देश तैयार किए जाते हैं / when the final specifications are drawn up
व्यवहार्यता अध्ययन के दौरान / during feasibility study
आवश्यकताओं विनिर्देशों चरण के दौरान / during requirements specifications stage
सिस्टम अध्ययन चरण के दौरान / during system study stage

technical_proof: The test plan is specified once the final system specifications are drawn up, since testing criteria depend on knowing the finalized requirements/design to test against.
explanation: You can only define a meaningful test plan after you know exactly what the final system is supposed to do — hence it follows final specification finalization.
trap_point: Students may guess 'during requirements specifications stage' (option c) assuming testing planning starts early — but formal test plans need FINAL specs, not draft ones.
memory_trick: You can't test against a plan until the final spec exists — Test plan follows Final Specs.
revision_fact: System test plans are specified once final specifications are finalized.

question_hindi: ___ का अर्थ है समन्वित प्रयास, लिखित रूप में सिस्टम की जानकारी को संप्रेषित करना।
question_english: ___ means coordinated effort to communicate the information of the system in written form.
technical_proof: System Documentation is the coordinated, organized written record that communicates all details about the system to stakeholders.
explanation: This matches the general definition of documentation as a formal record/communication vehicle throughout SDLC.
trap_point: 'User Document' (option d) is a narrower subtype — the question asks about the broader concept, so 'System documentation' is the better general answer.
memory_trick: Coordinated + written + about-the-system = System Documentation.
revision_fact: System documentation is the coordinated written communication of system information.

question_hindi: Analysis चरण में, ___ का विकास होता है, जो परियोजना के लक्ष्यों और उद्देश्यों का एक स्पष्ट विवरण है।
question_english: In the Analysis phase, the development of the ___ occurs, which is a clear statement of the goals and objectives of the project.
technical_proof: During Analysis, the Program Specification is developed — a clear statement outlining project goals/objectives that guides subsequent design work.
explanation: This is a defined output artifact of the Analysis phase per the standard SDLC breakdown used in this syllabus.
trap_point: Don't confuse with 'design' (option d), which is a later phase output, not an Analysis-phase artifact.
memory_trick: Analysis phase output = Program Specification (goals/objectives clarified).
revision_fact: Program specification, stating project goals/objectives, is developed during the Analysis phase.

question_hindi: Actual programming of software code किस SDLC चरण के दौरान किया जाता है?
question_english: Actual programming of software code is done during the ___ step in the SDLC.
technical_proof: Actual coding/programming happens in the 'Development and Documentation' step of the SDLC, where design is translated into working software code.
explanation: This SDLC model groups coding together with documentation as a single combined phase, distinct from Design (planning) and Analysis (requirements).
trap_point: Students may pick 'Design' thinking design and coding are the same phase — but coding is a distinct, later step (Development).
memory_trick: Design = blueprint; Development = actual code written.
revision_fact: Actual software coding occurs during the Development and Documentation phase of SDLC.

question_hindi: Enhancements, upgrades, और bug fixes किस SDLC चरण में किए जाते हैं?
question_english: Enhancements, upgrades, and bug fixes are done during the ___ step in the SDLC.
technical_proof: Post-deployment enhancements, upgrades, and bug fixes are activities of the Maintenance and Evaluation phase — the final, ongoing stage of the SDLC.
explanation: Maintenance is the phase after implementation, dealing with the system's operational life, including corrections and improvements.
trap_point: Straightforward — bug fixes/enhancements are classic 'maintenance' keywords, low distractor risk.
memory_trick: Bug fixes/upgrades AFTER launch = Maintenance phase.
revision_fact: Enhancements, upgrades, and bug fixes belong to the Maintenance and Evaluation phase.

question_hindi: एक rectangle DFD में क्या दर्शाता है?
question_english: A rectangle in a DFD represents.
technical_proof: Consistent with Q6 — a rectangle in DFD notation represents an External Entity (source/destination of data outside the system).
explanation: This reinforces standard DFD symbol conventions taught throughout the chapter.
trap_point: Repeat concept of Q6 — a very frequently repeated question type in this exam.
memory_trick: Rectangle = External Entity (memorize this pairing firmly, it repeats often).
revision_fact: DFD Rectangle symbol = External Entity.

question_hindi: जिस कोड को किसी वस्तु के मापने योग्य गुणों के साथ विकसित किया जाता है, उसे ___ कहा जाता है।
question_english: The code developed with the measurable properties of an item is known as ___.
technical_proof: A Significant Digit Code embeds actual measurable characteristics of the item (e.g., size, weight, dimension digits) directly into the code value.
explanation: Unlike serial or block codes, each digit/portion of a significant digit code carries real measurable meaning about the item it represents.
trap_point: Confused with 'Self checking code' — that's about error detection (like a check digit), not measurable properties.
memory_trick: Significant Digit Code = code digits ARE the measurements.
revision_fact: Significant digit codes encode measurable properties of the item directly into the code.

question_hindi: ___ किसी संगठन की संरचना को निर्दिष्ट करता है।
question_english: ___ specifies the structure of an organization.
technical_proof: An Organization Chart is specifically designed to depict the hierarchical/reporting structure of an organization.
explanation: This is a direct, unambiguous definitional match.
trap_point: DFD models data/process flow, not organizational hierarchy — easy elimination.
memory_trick: Org structure → Organization Chart, always.
revision_fact: Organization charts specify the structural hierarchy of an organization.

question_hindi: Structured Analysis के प्रमुख लक्ष्य कौनसे हैं-
question_english: Structured analysis's main goals are-
technical_proof: Structured Analysis aims to (i) explain to users via graphics, (ii) show a clear logical/physical divide, and (iii) produce system flowcharts - all three are recognized goals.
explanation: This combines communication clarity, abstraction separation, and visual documentation as joint objectives of structured analysis.
trap_point: Students may drop one goal thinking only 2 apply; the book key confirms all three.
memory_trick: Structured Analysis = Graphics + Logical/Physical split + Flowcharts.
revision_fact: Structured Analysis goals: user-friendly graphics, logical-physical clarity, flowchart creation.

question_hindi: Structured tools का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है-
question_english: What is the main objective of structured tools?
technical_proof: Structured tools collectively include DFD, Data Dictionary, and Decision Tables/Trees - each serving the shared goal of structured analysis/design.
explanation: These three are the classic 'structured tools' trio taught together in SAD.
trap_point: None - a clean 'all of the above' recognition question.
memory_trick: Structured tools trio: DFD + Data Dictionary + Decision Tables/Trees.
revision_fact: Structured tools = DFD, Data Dictionary, and Decision Tables collectively.

question_hindi: System design में efficiency में क्या देखा जाता है-
question_english: In system design, what is looked at for efficiency?
technical_proof: Efficiency in system design is judged by (i) Accuracy, (ii) Time, and (iii) Comprehensiveness; (iv) 'Strong' is not a standard efficiency criterion.
explanation: 'Strong' is a vague, non-technical term inserted as a distractor - not part of the standard efficiency criteria list.
trap_point: Avoid picking option combinations that include 'Strong' - it's not a recognized efficiency metric in SAD.
memory_trick: Efficiency = Accuracy + Time + Comprehensiveness (not 'Strong').
revision_fact: System design efficiency is judged on accuracy, time, and comprehensiveness.

question_hindi: Functional decomposition में Module को किसके द्वारा दर्शाया जाता है-
question_english: In functional decomposition, a Module is represented by-
technical_proof: In structure charts (functional decomposition diagrams), a Module is depicted using a rectangle box.
explanation: This mirrors general convention where boxes represent discrete functional units/modules in hierarchy diagrams.
trap_point: Don't confuse module notation (rectangle) with DFD process notation (circle) - different diagram types use different shapes for different meanings.
memory_trick: Structure Chart Module = Rectangle box (same shape family as DFD entity, but different diagram/meaning).
revision_fact: In functional decomposition/structure charts, a module is shown as a rectangle.

question_hindi: Advantages of system flowcharts ....................
question_english: Advantages of system flowcharts ....................
technical_proof: Per the book's key, 'Effective communication' is the selected primary advantage of system flowcharts (visualizing flow aids stakeholder communication).
explanation: System flowcharts are valued mainly for making data/process flow easy to communicate to non-technical stakeholders.
trap_point: Option (c) 'Queasier group or relationships' appears to be an OCR-garbled/nonsensical phrase; treat with caution.
memory_trick: Flowchart's #1 advantage: it communicates flow visually and effectively.
revision_fact: The primary advantage of system flowcharts is effective communication of process flow.

question_hindi: Information requirements of an organization can be determined by ___?
question_english: Information requirements of an organization can be determined by ___?

options.text: interviewing managers and users and arriving at requirements based on consensus
finding out what similar organizations do
telling organization what they need based on your experience
sending a questionnaire to all employees of the organization

technical_proof: The best-practice approach is interviewing stakeholders (managers/users) and building consensus, rather than copying other organizations or imposing analyst assumptions.
explanation: Options b, c, and d represent poor/unreliable practices (mimicry, analyst bias, blanket questionnaires without follow-up) compared to consensus-based interviewing.
trap_point: Sending a mass questionnaire (d) sounds thorough but lacks the interactive consensus-building that proper requirement determination needs.
memory_trick: Best requirement gathering = Interview + Consensus, not copy-paste or guesswork.
revision_fact: Information requirements are best determined through interviews with managers/users reaching consensus.

question_hindi: To create a vehicle of information to provide evidence in the development process and to monitor the process - this is one objective of ___.
question_english: To create a vehicle of information to provide evidence in the development process and to monitor the process. This is one of the objectives of ___.
technical_proof: Providing an evidentiary, monitorable information record throughout development is a core objective of Documentation.
explanation: Documentation exists precisely to serve as the traceable record/evidence trail across the SDLC.
trap_point: Students may pick 'Development' thinking of the coding phase, but the described purpose (evidence + monitoring) is specifically documentation's job.
memory_trick: Evidence + Monitoring record = Documentation's objective.
revision_fact: Documentation objectives include providing evidence and enabling process monitoring.

question_hindi: किसी भी input record या किसी system पर अपने original source पर वापस की गयी process का पता लगाना क्या कहलाता है-
question_english: Tracing back a process on any input record or system to its original source is called-
technical_proof: Tracing a transaction/process back to its source is the definition of an Audit Trail (spelled 'Audit trial' in the source due to OCR/typo).
explanation: Audit trails allow verification and accountability by linking outputs back to their originating inputs.
trap_point: Note: the book spells it 'Audit trial' - the correct standard term is 'Audit Trail'; treat as a spelling variant, not a different concept.
memory_trick: Tracing back to source = Audit Trail.
revision_fact: Audit trail = tracing a process/record back to its original source.
ocr_confidence: Medium - book spells term 'Audit trial', correct term is 'Audit Trail'

question_hindi: Decision table का उपयोग क्यों करते हैं-
question_english: Why is a Decision table used?

options.text: Information data को tabular form में displayed करने के लिए
Decision path को displayed करने के लिए
System के सही diagram को प्राप्त करने के लिए

technical_proof: Decision tables are used to display conditions/decision logic in a compact tabular format for information/data representation.
explanation: Per the key, the tabular-display purpose (option a) is chosen over the decision-path display, which is more characteristic of a Decision Tree.
trap_point: Careful: Decision Tree (not Table) is typically associated with showing 'decision paths' visually - don't confuse the two tools.
memory_trick: Decision TABLE = tabular data; Decision TREE = branching path.
revision_fact: Decision tables primarily display information/conditions in tabular form.

question_hindi: Cost benefit analysis क्या है-
question_english: What is Cost benefit analysis?

options.text: Hardware तथा software की cost को estimate करना
Cost को benefit के साथ compare करना
Tangible तथा intangible घटकों का मूल्यांकन करना

technical_proof: Per the book's key, cost/benefit analysis is defined narrowly here as estimating hardware and software costs (though broader definitions include comparing cost vs benefit).
explanation: Note: many textbooks would prefer option (b) or (d) as the fuller definition of cost-benefit analysis; this book's key selects (a) specifically.
trap_point: Potentially debatable: the more complete/standard definition of Cost-Benefit Analysis is comparing costs against benefits (option b) or evaluating both tangible/intangible factors (option c), making 'All of above' (d) arguably more correct than (a) alone.
memory_trick: Cost-benefit analysis conventionally = compare cost vs. benefit, not just estimate cost.
revision_fact: Standard definition: Cost-Benefit Analysis compares project costs against expected benefits (tangible & intangible).

question_hindi: DFD का मुख्य रूप से उपयोग में लिया जाता है-
question_english: DFD is primarily used to-

options.text: Requirement specification को विस्तार से न्यूनतम level तक functionally रूप में अपघटित करता है
यह Design phase का प्रारम्भिक बिन्दु है
DFD रेखाओं के Bubbles की श्रेणी में बनाता है

technical_proof: DFDs decompose requirements to functional detail, act as a starting point for design, and organize the diagram as connected bubbles/lines - all describe DFD's role.
explanation: This is a composite summary of DFD's multiple functions across analysis and design phases.
trap_point: None major - options are complementary, not contradictory, supporting the 'All of above' answer.
memory_trick: DFD = Decomposition tool + Design starting point + Bubble/line notation.
revision_fact: DFDs functionally decompose requirements and serve as the starting point for design.

question_hindi: Data Flow Diagram में संकेत चिह्नों का मिलान कीजिए: a.Square, b.Straight line, c.Circle, d.Open Rectangle
question_english: Match the DFD symbols: a.Square, b.Straight line, c.Circle, d.Open Rectangle
technical_proof: Correct mapping: Square=Entity(ii), Straight line=Data flow(i), Circle=Data on process/processing(iv), Open Rectangle=Data storage(iii).
explanation: This reflects standard DFD notation: Square/Rectangle=External Entity, Line=Data Flow (with arrow), Circle=Process, Open-ended rectangle=Data Store.
trap_point: Very common source of confusion - memorize each shape-to-meaning pairing individually rather than by elimination.
memory_trick: Square=Entity, Line=Flow, Circle=Process, Open box=Store.
revision_fact: DFD symbols: Square=Entity, Line=Flow, Circle=Process, Open Rectangle=Data Store.

question_hindi: ___ is a tabular method for describing the logic of the decisions to be taken.
question_english: ___ is a tabular method for describing the logic of the decisions to be taken.
technical_proof: By definition, a Decision Table is the tabular technique for representing decision logic (conditions vs actions).
explanation: This directly matches the standard SAD definition of Decision Tables.
trap_point: Straightforward - 'tabular' is the key word pointing directly to 'Decision Table', not 'Decision Tree' (which is graphical/branching).
memory_trick: Tabular = Table (not Tree).
revision_fact: Decision Table = tabular representation of decision logic.

question_hindi: The approach used in top-down analysis and design is:
question_english: The approach used in top-down analysis and design is:

options.text: to identify the top level functions by combining many smaller components into a single entity
to prepare flow charts after programming has been completed
to identify a top level function and then create a hierarchy of lower-level modules and components.

technical_proof: Top-down design starts from a high-level (top) function and progressively breaks it into a hierarchy of smaller, lower-level modules - the opposite of bottom-up combination.
explanation: Option (a) describes bottom-up composition, which is the reverse process; top-down decomposes rather than combines.
trap_point: Easy to confuse top-down (decompose from top) with bottom-up (combine from bottom) - read the direction of the arrow carefully.
memory_trick: Top-Down = Big function → broken into smaller modules (decomposition, not combination).
revision_fact: Top-down design decomposes a top-level function into a hierarchy of smaller modules.

question_hindi: Prototyping में उपयोग लिए जाते हैं-
question_english: In Prototyping, which are used-
technical_proof: Rapid prototyping tools are typically Fourth Generation Languages (4GLs) that allow quick screen/report generation, unlike older procedural languages like BASIC/COBOL.
explanation: 4GLs (e.g., SQL-based report generators, RAD tools) are specifically designed to speed up prototype building, which is why they're favored in prototyping methodology.
trap_point: Older procedural languages (BASIC, COBOL) are not the typical tools associated with rapid prototyping.
memory_trick: Prototyping = fast tools = 4GLs.
revision_fact: Prototyping methodology commonly uses 4GLs (Fourth Generation Languages) for rapid development.

question_hindi: Interaction का अर्थ क्या है-
question_english: What does Interaction mean?

options.text: Unit system के components एक साथ मिल जुलकर काम करते हैं
System को order में व्यवस्थित करना
Organization के component एक-दूसरे पर निर्भर रहना
System के सभी component बिना जुड़े अपना अलग-अलग कार्य करें

technical_proof: Interaction refers to system components working jointly/together, i.e., mutual engagement between parts of the system.
explanation: This distinguishes 'Interaction' (components working together) from 'Interdependence' (components depending on each other, option c) - related but distinct system concepts.
trap_point: Confused with 'Interdependence' (option c) - Interaction is about joint working, Interdependence is about mutual reliance.
memory_trick: Interaction = components working TOGETHER (joint action).
revision_fact: Interaction means system components work together jointly.

question_hindi: निम्न में से acceptance testing कब किया जाता है-
question_english: When is acceptance testing done?

options.text: Running the system with live data by the actual user.
Testing change made in an existing or a new program
Is checking the logic of one or making program in the candidate system.

technical_proof: Per the book's key, acceptance testing covers running the system live with the actual user, testing changes to programs, and checking program logic - combined under 'All of the above'.
explanation: This is a broad, book-specific composite definition of acceptance testing covering multiple testing activities.
trap_point: Note: strictly, 'checking logic' (option c) more precisely describes unit/program testing rather than acceptance testing - but the book combines all as one answer; flagged for awareness, not overridden since it's the officially keyed answer.
memory_trick: Acceptance testing (classic definition) = running with live data by the ACTUAL USER.
revision_fact: Acceptance testing centrally involves the actual user testing the system with live/real data.

question_hindi: System Analysis में निम्न में से documentation कब prepared किया जाता है-
question_english: In System Analysis, when is documentation prepared?
technical_proof: Documentation is an ongoing activity carried out at every SDLC stage, not confined to a single phase.
explanation: This reinforces the concept from Q44/Q71 - documentation happens continuously throughout the lifecycle.
trap_point: Students might restrict documentation to just one phase (e.g., analysis) - but it truly spans all stages.
memory_trick: Documentation is a CONTINUOUS activity across all SDLC phases.
revision_fact: Documentation is prepared at every stage of system development, not just one.

question_hindi: किसी सॉफ्टवेयर कोड की वास्तविक प्रोग्रामिंग (Actual Programming) SDLC के किस चरण (step) में पूरी की जाती है-
question_english: During which SDLC step is actual programming of software code completed?
technical_proof: This repeats Q46's concept: actual coding happens in the Development and Documentation phase of SDLC.
explanation: Same underlying fact as Q46 - duplicate concept, different phrasing.
trap_point: Same trap as before: don't confuse Design (planning) with Development (actual coding).
memory_trick: Design = blueprint; Development = actual code (same as Q46).
revision_fact: Actual programming/coding is completed during Development and Documentation phase.

question_hindi: प्रोसेस SDLC के किस स्टेप में Enhancement, Update और Bug Fix प्रोसेस पूरी की जाती है-
question_english: In which SDLC step are the Enhancement, Update, and Bug Fix processes completed?
technical_proof: This repeats Q47's concept - enhancements/updates/bug fixes belong to the Maintenance and Evaluation phase.
explanation: Same underlying fact as Q47 - duplicate concept, different phrasing.
trap_point: Same trap as Q47: post-launch fixes are Maintenance activities, not Design/Analysis.
memory_trick: Bug fixes/updates AFTER launch = Maintenance phase (same as Q47).
revision_fact: Enhancement/update/bug fix work belongs to the Maintenance and Evaluation phase.

question_hindi: Documentation is prepared .............
question_english: Documentation is prepared .............
technical_proof: Consistent with Q44/Q68 - documentation is prepared continuously across every SDLC stage, not just one.
explanation: This is essentially a third repeat of the same continuous-documentation concept.
trap_point: Same trap - avoid isolating documentation to just one phase.
memory_trick: Documentation happens at EVERY stage (repeated concept, memorize firmly).
revision_fact: Documentation is prepared at every stage of the SDLC (frequently repeated fact).

question_hindi: Decision tree uses ...............
question_english: Decision tree uses ...............
technical_proof: A Decision Tree pictorially depicts alternate conditions using nodes and branches, and shows consequences of each alternative - all three features apply.
explanation: Decision trees combine graphical structure (nodes/branches) with logical representation (conditions/consequences).
trap_point: Contrast with Decision Table (Q59/Q63), which is tabular, not pictorial/branching.

question_hindi: Physical DFD क्या-क्या दर्शाता है-

question_hindi: Coupling किसे कहा जाता है-

Module को छोटे-छोटे modules में विभाजित करना

question_hindi: The problem statement includes the ___ which lists specific input numbers a program would typically expect the user to enter and precise output values that a perfect program would return for those input values.

revision_fact: The problem statement's input/output value listing supports building the testing plan.

question_hindi: ___ System is no more than idea.

revision_fact: A Conceptual system is merely an idea, prior to logical or physical development.

question_hindi: एक ऐसा program जो Coupling व Cohesion के मापदण्डों को पूरा करता है-

revision_fact: Programs satisfying coupling/cohesion standards are represented via hierarchy/structure charts.

question_hindi: ..... एक ग्राफिकल तकनीक है जो कंडीशन और एक्शन (Condition and action) को एक के बाद एक सीक्वेंस में प्रस्तुत करती है-

question_hindi: Project Schedule को चित्रित (represent) करने के लिए किस चार्ट का प्रयोग किया जाता है-

revision_fact: Gantt charts are used to represent project schedules.

question_hindi: कौनसा DFDs System में data के flow तथा System के process पर केंद्रित रहता है-

question_hindi: Problem analysis is done during ___.

memory_trick: Problem analysis = Analysis phase (before Design).
revision_fact: Problem analysis is conducted during the systems analysis phase.

question_hindi: A decision table facilitates conditions to be related to ___?
question_english: A decision table facilitates conditions to be related to ___?

revision_fact: Decision tables relate conditions to their corresponding actions.

question_hindi: निम्न में से कौनसा data file, multiple data file को contain करता है-

memory_trick: Index-Sequential = Index file + Sequential file combined.
revision_fact: Index-sequential files combine sequential and index file structures together.

question_hindi: निम्नलिखित file में से least file कौनसा है-
question_english: Which of the following is the 'least' (smallest/most transient) file?

trap_point: Don't confuse 'least' (temporary/least persistent) with 'least important' - it's about data permanence/lifespan.
memory_trick: Working file = shortest-lived, most temporary file type.
revision_fact: Working files are the most transient/temporary among common file types.

question_hindi: A ___ is an outline of a process that develops successful information systems.

question_hindi: The problem statement should include all of the following EXCEPT.
question_english: The problem statement should include all of the following EXCEPT.

revision_fact: Problem statements define input, processing, and output - not storage.

question_hindi: By an external entity we mean a ___.
question_english: By an external entity we mean a ___.

options.text: Unit outside the system being designed which can be controlled by an analyst.
Unit outside the system whose behavior is independent of the system being designed
A unit external to the system being designed
A unit which is not part of a DFD

explanation: Options (a) and (b) add extra (incorrect) qualifiers - analysts don't 'control' external entities, and their behavior isn't necessarily fully independent; (c) is the cleanest correct definition.
trap_point: Don't over-qualify the definition with 'controlled by analyst' or 'fully independent behavior' - the simplest correct definition (just 'external to the system') is what's tested.
memory_trick: External Entity = simply anything OUTSIDE the system boundary.
revision_fact: An external entity is any unit external to the system being designed.

question_hindi: An appraisal of a system's performance after it has been installed is called ___.
question_english: An appraisal of a system's performance after it has been installed is called ___.

memory_trick: Post-install performance check often labeled 'Review', but this book groups it under Maintenance.
revision_fact: Post-installation performance appraisal falls under the Maintenance & Evaluation phase per this source.

question_hindi: An example of a hierarchical data structure is ___?
question_english: An example of a hierarchical data structure is ___?

revision_fact: Tree is the hierarchical data structure among the given options.

question_hindi: Database system का क्या लाभ है-

question_hindi: SDLC का first step कौनसा है-

question_hindi: Which of the following is not a characteristic of good test data?

question_hindi: In the system concepts, term Integration ___.

question_hindi: Birth to Mature की प्रोसेस कहलाती है-

revision_fact: Enhancement in SDLC means increasing/improving the system.

question_hindi: System का मुख्य कार्य क्या है-

यह विभिन्न तत्वों का एक समूह होता है
एक organized समूह के सभी घटकों को एक function unit में जोड़ना

question_hindi: Translating the algorithm into a programming language occurs at the ___ step of the PDLC.

question_hindi: Error report is an example of ___.

question_hindi: System के लिए सही कथन है-

System किसी process को पूरा नहीं करता
System के प्रत्येक component का अपना कार्य होता है

technical_proof: Standard systems theory holds that a system DOES perform/complete processes (transformation of inputs to outputs) to achieve its objective - statement (c) as commonly read would be FALSE, not true.

memory_trick: Systems DO perform processes - don't accept 'system does not complete a process' as true.
revision_fact: Systems perform transformation processes on inputs to produce outputs; claiming otherwise is factually incorrect.

question_hindi: The rules to follow in constructing decision tables is (are):
question_english: The rules to follow in constructing decision tables is (are):

the logic of the table is independent of the sequence in which conditions rules are written, but the action takes place in the order in which the events occur.

revision_fact: Decision table construction follows naming, logic-independence, and standardized language rules.

question_hindi: ___ एक संगठित परिवर्तन प्रक्रिया में आदानों को स्वीकार करके और आउटपुट का उत्पादन करके एक सामान्य लक्ष्य की दिशा में एक साथ काम करने वाले इच्छुक घटकों का एक समूह है।

revision_fact: A system transforms inputs into outputs via organized, goal-directed components.

question_hindi: समस्या कथन को प्रोग्राम को क्या करना चाहिए इसका वर्णन करने वाले क्रमिक चरणों की एक श्रृंखला में अनुवाद करना ___ के रूप में जाना जाता है।

revision_fact: Creating the algorithm = translating the problem into sequential logical steps.

question_hindi: DFD में डेटा स्टोर दर्शाता है-

question_hindi: DFD में एक आयत ___ दर्शाता है?

question_hindi: System का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है-

revision_fact: A system's objectives include both achieving predetermined goals and maintaining component interlinking.

question_hindi: एक संक्षिप्त कोड (concise code) अनिवार्य रूप से है-

question_hindi: External Entities may be-

question_hindi: It is necessary to prioritize information requirements of an organization at the requirements determination phase as-
