question_hindi: डिबगिंग है:
question_english: Debugging is:

options.text: प्रोग्राम कोड बनाना / creating program code
प्रोग्राम कोड में त्रुटियों को ढूँढना और सुधारना / finding and correcting errors in the program code
कम्प्यूटरीकृत किए जाने वाले कार्य की पहचान करना / identifying the task to be computerized

technical_proof: Debugging is precisely the process of finding and fixing errors ('bugs') in program code, distinct from writing code, algorithm design, or task identification.
explanation: This is a direct definitional match with no ambiguity.
trap_point: None - clean, unambiguous vocabulary question.
memory_trick: Debugging = Find + Fix errors (not creating code).
revision_fact: Debugging is finding and correcting errors in program code.

question_hindi: फीचर ओरिएंटेड डोमेन एनालिसिस (FODA) में कितने चरण शामिल हैं?
question_english: How many steps are involved in Feature Oriented Domain Analysis (FODA)?
technical_proof: FODA (Feature Oriented Domain Analysis) is described in this syllabus as consisting of 3 steps/phases of domain analysis.
explanation: This is a specific methodology fact tied to domain engineering approaches referenced in the SAD syllabus.
trap_point: Less commonly known fact - worth memorizing directly as it's easy to guess incorrectly (2, 4, or 5).
memory_trick: FODA = 3 steps (memorize directly).
revision_fact: FODA (Feature Oriented Domain Analysis) has 3 steps.

question_hindi: ___ system में programs, data files और documentation शामिल हैं।
question_english: ___ system consists of programs, data files and documentation.
technical_proof: A Physical system is the concrete, implemented system that actually contains real programs, data files, and documentation - unlike Conceptual (idea) or Logical (abstract design) systems.
explanation: This distinguishes the three system-development stages: Conceptual (idea) → Logical (design) → Physical (real, implemented with actual files/programs).
trap_point: Don't confuse with 'Logical', which is still an abstract design blueprint, not the actual implemented programs/files.
memory_trick: Physical = REAL, implemented system with actual files/programs (final concrete stage).
revision_fact: A Physical system contains actual programs, data files, and documentation.

question_hindi: एक आवश्यकता विनिर्देश तैयार करने वाले सिस्टम विश्लेषक की भूमिका किसके समान है?
question_english: The role of a system analyst drawing up a requirements specification is similar to ?

options.text: a structural engineer designing a building
the workers who construct a building

technical_proof: A systems analyst drafting requirements is analogous to an Architect, who plans/designs based on client needs before construction begins - not the builder/contractor who executes.
explanation: This is a classic analogy used in SAD teaching to explain the analyst's planning (not implementation) role.
trap_point: Don't confuse with 'contractor' or 'workers' (implementation roles) - the analyst's role is analogous to planning/design, like an architect.
memory_trick: Analyst = Architect (plans/designs), not Contractor/Workers (who build).
revision_fact: A systems analyst's role parallels an architect's role - planning and designing before construction/implementation.

question_hindi: Open या Close System की प्रमुख विशेषता है-
question_english: The major characteristics of an Open or Closed System are-
technical_proof: Per the book's key, Entropy (1) and Equifinality (2) are the key characteristics highlighted here, while Input from outside (3) and Transmission (4) are excluded from this particular pairing.
explanation: Entropy (tendency toward disorder) and Equifinality (reaching the same end state via different paths) are classic systems-theory concepts often discussed together for open/closed systems.
trap_point: This is a somewhat book-specific selection; standard theory would note that 'input from outside' (3) is actually a defining trait of OPEN systems specifically - but the book's key pairs (1) and (2) together for this general question.
memory_trick: Entropy + Equifinality are commonly paired systems-theory concepts (per this book).
revision_fact: Entropy and Equifinality are highlighted as key general systems characteristics in this source.
ocr_confidence: Medium - question conflates open/closed system traits, book-specific answer selection

question_hindi: ऐसा कोई real object जो operation की दृष्टि से static या dynamic हो ___ कहलाता है-
question_english: Any real object that is static or dynamic from an operational viewpoint is called-
technical_proof: A Physical system refers to any real, tangible object/system, which may be static or dynamic depending on its operational behavior - a broad classification distinct from open/closed system theory.
explanation: This defines 'Physical system' as the real-world counterpart to abstract/conceptual systems, regardless of its static or dynamic nature.
trap_point: Don't confuse with Open/Closed classification (which is about environment interaction, not real-vs-abstract nature).
memory_trick: Physical system = REAL object (static or dynamic), as opposed to abstract/conceptual.
revision_fact: A physical system is any real object, whether static or dynamic in operation.

question_hindi: ___ is the process of translating a task into a series of commands that a computer will use to perform that task.
question_english: ___ is the process of translating a task into a series of commands that a computer will use to perform that task.
technical_proof: Converting a task into computer-executable commands is the definition of Programming.
explanation: This is a direct, unambiguous definitional match.
trap_point: None - straightforward definitional question.
memory_trick: Task → Computer commands = Programming.
revision_fact: Programming translates a task into a series of computer-executable commands.

question_hindi: ___ is a good example of deterministic system.
question_english: ___ is a good example of deterministic system.
technical_proof: A Computer Program is deterministic - given the same input, it always produces the same, predictable output, following fixed logic without randomness.
explanation: Deterministic systems have fully predictable behavior, which is the defining trait of standard computer program execution.
trap_point: Note: 'Software Program' (option c) is very similar wording to 'Computer Program' (option b) - the book's key specifically selects (b); read carefully.
memory_trick: Deterministic = predictable output for given input = Computer Program.
revision_fact: A computer program is a classic example of a deterministic system.

question_hindi: आवश्यकता विनिर्देश तैयार करते समय निम्नलिखित से परामर्श करना आवश्यक है?
question_english: It is necessary to consult the following while drawing up requirement specification?

options.text: only top, middle and operational managers
top, middle and operational managers and also all who will use the system

technical_proof: Requirement specification should consult ALL levels of management AND all actual system users - a narrow consultation (only managers) risks missing critical operational/user-level needs.
explanation: This reflects best-practice requirement gathering: comprehensive stakeholder engagement across all organizational levels plus end-users.
trap_point: Students may pick a narrower option assuming only managers matter, but end-users (who directly use the system) must also be consulted.
memory_trick: Consult EVERYONE: Top + Middle + Operational + Actual Users.
revision_fact: Requirement specification must consult all management levels plus all system users.

question_hindi: Structured analysis में उपयोग ली जाने वाली chart तकनीक कौन-कौनसी हैं-
question_english: Which chart techniques are used in Structured analysis?
technical_proof: Per the book's key, Bar chart (i) and Line chart (ii) are the chart techniques selected as used in structured analysis; Circle chart (iii) and 'Square chart' (iv, a fictitious type from Q14) are excluded.
explanation: This aligns with Q14's earlier fact that 'Square chart' isn't a real chart type, reinforcing why option combinations including (iv) are wrong.
trap_point: Remember from Q14 that 'Square chart' doesn't exist - eliminate any option containing (iv).
memory_trick: Bar + Line charts are the valid structured-analysis chart types here; avoid the fictitious 'Square chart'.
revision_fact: Structured analysis commonly uses Bar and Line chart techniques (per this source).

question_hindi: Bubble Chart का अन्य नाम है-
question_english: Another name for Bubble Chart is-
technical_proof: 'Bubble Chart' is an alternate/informal name for the Data Flow Diagram (DFD), so-called because processes are drawn as circles/'bubbles'.
explanation: This is a well-known nickname for DFDs due to their circular process symbols.
trap_point: None - direct terminology match, low risk.
memory_trick: Bubble Chart = nickname for DFD (because processes look like bubbles/circles).
revision_fact: 'Bubble Chart' is another name for Data Flow Diagram.

question_hindi: In order to understand the working of an organization for which a computer based system is being designed, an analyst must ___?
question_english: In order to understand the working of an organization for which a computer based system is being designed, an analyst must ___?

options.text: look at only current work and document flow in the organization
discuss with top level and middle level management only
interview top, middle line managers and also clerks who will enter data and use the System
only clerical and middle level staff who have long experience in the organization and will be users of the system

technical_proof: A thorough analyst interviews ALL levels - top, middle managers, and clerks/end-users - to understand the organization fully, not just management or just clerical staff alone.
explanation: Comprehensive fact-finding requires input from every stakeholder level, similar to the logic in Q118.
trap_point: Avoid narrow options that restrict consultation to only management or only clerical staff - full-spectrum interviewing is the correct practice.
memory_trick: Interview EVERYONE across all levels (same principle as Q118).
revision_fact: Analysts must interview all organizational levels - top, middle, and clerical/operational staff - to understand the organization.

question_hindi: ___ manages the system development, assign staff, manage the budget and reporting, and ensure that deadlines are met.
question_english: ___ manages the system development, assign staff, manage the budget and reporting, and ensure that deadlines are met.
technical_proof: Managing staff assignment, budget, reporting, and deadlines are core responsibilities of a Project Manager, distinct from the technical/analytical role of a Systems Analyst.
explanation: This differentiates Project Manager (administrative/managerial oversight) from Systems Analyst (requirements/design focus, see Q127, Q144).
trap_point: Don't confuse with 'Systems analysts' (option d) - analysts handle requirements/design, project managers handle budget/staffing/deadlines.
memory_trick: Budget + Staff + Deadlines = Project Manager's job (not the Analyst's).
revision_fact: Project managers oversee staffing, budget, reporting, and deadlines in system development.

question_hindi: The main ingredient of the report documenting the ........... is benefit analysis.
question_english: The main ingredient of the report documenting the ........... is benefit analysis.
technical_proof: The Feasibility Study report's main ingredient is benefit analysis (alongside cost analysis), since feasibility is fundamentally about weighing costs against benefits.
explanation: This connects to Economic Feasibility's cost-benefit focus (see Q19, Q21, Q60).
trap_point: None - direct, logical connection to feasibility study's core purpose.
memory_trick: Feasibility Study report's core ingredient = Benefit (Cost/Benefit) Analysis.
revision_fact: Benefit analysis is a core ingredient of the Feasibility Study report.

question_hindi: A feasibility study is carried out ___?
question_english: A feasibility study is carried out ___?

options.text: after final requirements specifications are drawn up
during the period when requirements specifications are drawn up
before the final requirements specifications are drawn up

technical_proof: Feasibility study is conducted BEFORE final requirements specifications are drawn up - it determines whether the project should proceed at all, prior to detailed requirement finalization.
explanation: This establishes the correct SDLC ordering: Feasibility Study → Requirements Specification → Design → etc.
trap_point: Don't confuse with 'after final specs' (option a) - feasibility comes first, as a go/no-go gate before detailed specs are finalized.
memory_trick: Feasibility Study happens BEFORE final requirement specs are locked in.
revision_fact: Feasibility studies are conducted before final requirements specifications are finalized.

question_hindi: The main objective of feasibility study is ___.
question_english: The main objective of feasibility study is ___.

options.text: to assess whether it is possible to meet the requirements specifications
to assess if it is possible to meet the requirements specified subject to constraints of budget, human resource and hardware
to assist the management in implementing the desired system
to remove bottlenecks in implementing the desired system

technical_proof: Feasibility study's main objective is assessing whether requirements can be met WITHIN REAL CONSTRAINTS (budget, HR, hardware) - not just checking requirements in isolation.
explanation: Option (a) is too simplistic (ignoring constraints); (b) captures the full, realistic scope of feasibility assessment.
trap_point: Watch for the more 'complete' sounding option that includes constraint awareness (b) versus a partial/incomplete version (a).
memory_trick: Feasibility = Can requirements be met, GIVEN real constraints (budget/HR/hardware)?
revision_fact: Feasibility study assesses if requirements can be met within budget, human resource, and hardware constraints.

question_hindi: System Study में शामिल होता है-
question_english: System Study includes-

options.text: मौजूदा प्रणाली का अध्ययन (Study of an existing system)
मौजूदा प्रणाली का डॉक्यूमेंटेशन (Documentation of existing system)
मौजूदा प्रणाली की कमियों को पहचानना (Identifying current deficiencies)

technical_proof: System Study encompasses studying the existing system, documenting it, and identifying its deficiencies - all three are core components of this stage.
explanation: This is consistent with Feasibility Study's review scope described earlier (Q29).
trap_point: None - composite, complementary options question.
memory_trick: System Study = Study existing + Document it + Find its flaws.
revision_fact: System Study includes studying, documenting, and identifying deficiencies of the existing system.

question_hindi: ___ spend most of their time in the beginning stages of the SDLC, talking with end-users, gathering information, documenting systems, and proposing solutions.
question_english: ___ spend most of their time in the beginning stages of the SDLC, talking with end-users, gathering information, documenting systems, and proposing solutions.
technical_proof: Talking to end-users, gathering info, documenting, and proposing solutions in the early SDLC stages are core Systems Analyst activities.
explanation: This complements Q122's distinction - Analysts focus on requirements/solutions, while Project Managers handle budget/staffing/deadlines.
trap_point: Don't confuse with Project Manager (Q122) - here the focus is on requirement-gathering/proposing solutions, which is the Analyst's domain.
memory_trick: Early SDLC + talking to users + gathering info = Systems Analyst's job.
revision_fact: Systems analysts spend early SDLC stages gathering info and proposing solutions with end-users.

question_hindi: A data flow can-
question_english: A data flow can-

options.text: Enter or leave a data Store
Either enter or leave a data store but not both

technical_proof: Mirrors Q24's rule for external entities - a single data flow arrow to/from a data store is one-directional: either entering OR leaving, not both simultaneously.
explanation: This reinforces the general DFD convention that individual data flow arrows represent one-directional movement only.
trap_point: Same trap as Q24 - don't assume a single flow arrow can represent bidirectional movement.
memory_trick: One flow arrow = ONE direction only (same rule as Q24 for entities).
revision_fact: A data flow either enters or leaves a data store, never both in a single flow.

question_hindi: System designing हेतु प्रयुक्त SDLC का Second step कौनसा होता है-
question_english: What is the Second step of SDLC used for System designing?
technical_proof: Per the book's key, after Initial Investigation (step 1), System Analysis is treated as the second step of the SDLC sequence in this syllabus.
explanation: This SDLC sequence is: Initial Investigation → System Analysis → Design → Development → Testing → Implementation → Maintenance (per this book's model).
trap_point: SDLC step numbering can vary slightly by textbook; here Analysis directly follows Initial Investigation as step 2.
memory_trick: SDLC order (this book): Initial Investigation (1) → Analysis (2) → ...

question_hindi: Changing the relationship with and services provided to customers in such a way that they will not think of changing suppliers is called ___.
question_english: Changing the relationship with and services provided to customers in such a way that they will not think of changing suppliers is called ___.
technical_proof: This describes a 'Customer Lock-in' strategy - making it costly/inconvenient for customers to switch to a competing supplier, thereby retaining them.
explanation: This is a strategic information systems concept about building customer loyalty/dependency through improved services.
trap_point: Don't confuse with 'Lock out' terms, which refer to blocking competitors, not retaining customers.
memory_trick: Keeping customers from LEAVING = Lock IN customers.
revision_fact: Lock-in customers strategy retains customers by making switching suppliers unattractive.

question_hindi: ___ को डेटा के रूप में परिभाषित किया जा सकता है जिसे एक ऐसे रूप में संसाधित किया गया है जो प्राप्तकर्ता के लिए सार्थक है और वर्तमान या संभावित निर्णयों में वास्तविक या अनुमानित मूल्य का है।
question_english: ___ can be defined as data that has been processed into a form that is meaningful to the recipient and is of real or perceived value in current or prospective decisions.

explanation: Duplicate concept of Q9, phrased identically.
trap_point: Same as Q9 - Data is raw, Information is processed/meaningful.
memory_trick: Information = Processed + Meaningful + Decision-valuable data (repeated fact).
revision_fact: Information is meaningfully processed data with decision-making value (repeated definition).

question_hindi: It is necessary to carry out a feasibility study as ___.
question_english: It is necessary to carry out a feasibility study as ___.

options.text: top management cannot ensure that a project is feasible before calling a system analyst
top management is not sure what they want from the system
even though top management is in favour of the system, technology may not be mature for implementation

technical_proof: A feasibility study is necessary precisely because top management alone cannot guarantee a project's viability without expert (system analyst) assessment - this justifies the analyst-led feasibility process.
explanation: This highlights the analyst's essential role in objectively validating feasibility, which management cannot self-certify.
trap_point: Options (b) and (c) sound plausible but describe specific scenarios/symptoms, not the general justification the book's key selects.
memory_trick: Feasibility study exists because management CAN'T self-verify project viability - needs expert analysis.
revision_fact: Feasibility studies are necessary because management alone cannot ensure project feasibility without analyst input.

question_hindi: Feasibility study is carried out by ___?
question_english: Feasibility study is carried out by ___?

options.text: system analyst in consultation with managers of the organization
systems designers in consultation with prospective users of the system

technical_proof: Feasibility studies are conducted by the System Analyst working WITH organizational managers - a collaborative process, not done solely by either party alone.
explanation: This reflects the analyst's central role in feasibility assessment, informed by management input (consistent with Q132's reasoning).
trap_point: Don't pick 'managers alone' (a) or 'analyst alone' implied by other options - it's specifically a joint analyst-manager consultation.
memory_trick: Feasibility Study = Analyst + Manager consultation (joint effort).
revision_fact: Feasibility study is conducted by the system analyst in consultation with organizational managers.

question_hindi: सिस्टम डिफाइनिंग में प्रयुक्त ऐसा सिस्टम जो अपने बाहर के वातावरण (Environment) से interact नहीं करता ... सिस्टम कहलाता है-
question_english: In system defining, a system that does not interact with its outside environment is called a ___ system.
technical_proof: A Closed system, by definition, does not exchange inputs/outputs with its external environment - it is self-contained.
explanation: This is the standard systems-theory contrast with Open systems (Q135), which do interact with their environment.
trap_point: Straightforward pairing question with Q135 - make sure to match 'no interaction' to Closed, and 'interaction' to Open.
memory_trick: Closed = NO interaction with environment; Open = interacts with environment.
revision_fact: A Closed system does not interact with its external environment.

question_hindi: ऐसा सिस्टम जो अपने बाहर के वातावरण (environment) से इंटैक्ट करता है ___ सिस्टम कहलाता है-
question_english: A system that interacts with its outside environment is called a ___ system.

trap_point: Direct complement of Q134 - remember these two definitions as a pair.
memory_trick: Open = interacts with environment; Closed = does not (paired concept with Q134).
revision_fact: An Open system interacts with its external environment.

question_hindi: Fact finding process के लिए निम्न में से कौनसी तकनीक इस्तेमाल की जाती है-

revision_fact: Database Administrators specialize in designing and implementing database structures.

question_hindi: Increased volume of sales किस Benefit का उदाहरण है। Reduction of bad debts किसका उदाहरण है?

question_hindi: ....... फिजिबिलिटी में अनुमानित लाभों (Estimated profit) की तुलना अनुमानित लागत (estimated cost) से की जाती है-

revision_fact: Initial requirements specification is only a rough indication, refined later into final specs.

question_hindi: सिस्टम से जुड़ी सभी बातें एक अरेंज फॉर्म में .... लिखी जाती हैं-

question_hindi: निम्नलिखित System testing का उद्देश्य क्या है-

revision_fact: System testing covers online response, volume, and stress testing objectives.

question_english: Final specifications are drawn up by ___.

options.text: system analyst in consultation with the management of the organization
system analyst in consultation with programmers

question_hindi: System user से बात करके जानकारी इकट्ठा करना, डॉक्यूमेंटेशन करना, सिस्टम डिजाईन तैयार करना आदि कार्य कौन करता है-

question_hindi: Technical writers generally provide the ___ for the new system.
